slots.subtopic: Work done by friction on incline
slots.brief: A block released from rest slides down a long rough incline of known incline angle and friction coefficient; find fraction of initial energy lost to heat, using work-energy theorem with friction.
A pendulum taken to a planet with given combination of g and length change; compute percentage/ratio change in time period using T ∝ sqrt(l/g).
A rod fixed between rigid walls is heated through a known ΔT; find compressive thermal stress using Y and α, possibly combined with a rise in temperature at which stress equals breaking stress.
A source moving between two observers (approach and recede) or observer moving both ways; set up Doppler ratios and find source speed from ratio of the two apparent frequencies.
Two bodies dropped/thrown from top of a tower at different times; use two simultaneous equations to find time when they meet or height of tower.
Find flux through one face of a cube/cubical arrangement with a charge placed at centre or corner or on a face; use symmetry division plus Gauss's law reasoning.
At same temperature compare rms speeds of two gases of given molar masses; extend to find temperature at which a lighter gas matches rms speed of a heavier one.
A wire is stretched to double (or n-times) its length keeping volume constant; find new resistance and ratio of old to new resistance.
Two capacitors (charged and uncharged, or at different voltages) connected in parallel; find charge redistributed and fraction of stored energy lost.
Given ratio of radii of two planets and escape-orbit data, compare g at surfaces using g ∝ ρR or GM/R² with density given; ratio comparison question.
Ice at known mass and temperature mixed with water/steam in a calorimeter; use latent heat plus specific heat in a chain to find final temperature or mass of ice remaining.
A particle at a given position with given velocity experiences a force; compute torque r × F and angular momentum r × mv about origin and check their relation.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slots.brief: Compare de Broglie wavelengths of an electron accelerated through given p.d. vs a proton/alpha with same KE; multi-step ratio with sqrt(m) scaling.

slots.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slots.brief: Four statements on degrees of freedom, equipartition, mean free path dependence, or KE vs temperature for ideal gases; identify the correct ones (multi-true conceptual at high difficulty).
Given x(t) or y(x) trajectory form, extract parameters (u, angle, time of flight) and compute range or maximum height; moderately involved standard-form comparison.
A block on a smooth incline inside a lift accelerating upward with known a; resolve forces along/perpendicular to incline and find acceleration relative to incline.
A charged particle enters at angle to a uniform B field; find pitch and radius of helical path, and how pitch changes if speed/angle/B is altered.

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: Magnetic field at centre of a regular polygonal coil (square/hexagon) of N turns with current I; direct superposition formula or comparison of square vs circular loop of same perimeter.
Zener diode regulator circuit with source, series resistance and load; find current through Zener and load, and power dissipated when input voltage varies (high difficulty numerical).
YDSE with slab introduced or source partially immersed: shift of fringe pattern; compute number of fringes shifted or new position of a maximum using extra path (μ−1)t.
Hydrogen atom in nth excited state emits radiation of given (longest/shortest) wavelength in a transition; count possible spectral lines or identify the transition using Bohr energy formula.
Direct one-step numerical: wire of given length, area, load hung from ceiling; find elongation or Young's modulus using Y = FL/(AΔL) with unit conversion.
Read amplitude, frequency, wave speed (from ω/k) from standard-form wave equation y = A sin(ωt − kx) and identify direction of propagation; simple read-off.
Convex/mirror problem: object at given distance, image formed on screen; use mirror formula and magnification to find focal length and image nature (two equations two unknowns).
A cycle composed of known segments (isobaric + isothermal/adiabatic) on a P–V diagram with numeric states; compute total work in cycle, heat in a branch, or efficiency using first law per branch.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Which of the given physical quantities are unchanged for a photon/electron if accelerating potential is doubled, or identify correct photoelectric statements (threshold, saturation current, stopping potential) as true/false.
Simple series LCR at resonance or given XL, XC, R: compute impedance or power factor directly by substitution; one-step plugging.
Battery of known emf and internal resistance connected across external resistor; find terminal voltage, current and power delivered — simple two-step circuit analysis.
V(x) given as polynomial function (e.g. ax² − bx); find electric field as function of x, locate point where E = 0, or evaluate field at a point by differentiation.
Given atomic masses of parent, daughter and alpha particle, compute Q-value/energy released in alpha decay using mass defect; medium-difficulty numerical.
Three/four point masses placed at corners of a square or along a rod; find coordinates of centre of mass by weighted average (simple direct computation).
Ratio of intensities at a point where two coherent waves meet with given phase difference (including cases beyond 90°/180°); compute Imax/Imin from amplitude ratio of interfering beams.
A loop/rail in a region where B varies with time (B = B0 + kt) or a rotating disc/rod: find induced emf via dΦ/dt with geometry, then current and power dissipated.

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: Light/EM wave of given intensity or power falls on a surface (reflecting/absorbing, possibly at angle); compute radiation pressure and force on the surface.
A chain of connected blocks on rough surfaces or a massive rope pulled over a pulley; write free-body equations for each and solve for tension at a point or acceleration (symbolic multi-equation).
Cylindrical vessel full of liquid rotated at angular speed ω; find height difference between edge and centre or pressure at a point using parabolic free-surface relation.
Given combination of gates feeding an output, construct truth table for all input combinations; identify equivalent single gate (NAND/NOR logic reduction).
A physical quantity computed from measured quantities (e.g. ρ = m/(4/3 πr³) or T = 2π√(l/g)); given percentage errors in measurements, find maximum percentage error in result.

A satellite in circular orbit or projectile from pole to surface: use conservation of mechanical energy with given orbital speed/radius to find escape velocity ratio or additional speed needed to escape.
Simple statement-selection: image formation plane mirror / total internal reflection conditions / power of lens in medium; pick correct statement among simple ray-optics assertions.

slots.archetype: Hess's law bond-energy calc combined with ΔH = ΔU + ΔnRT
slots.brief: Give a multi-step reaction cycle with a gaseous combustion step; ask for ΔU of the overall process using bond enthalpies plus the ΔH–ΔU conversion — hard bookkeeping.
Rank four alkyl/benzyl halides in order of SN1 reactivity, including one aryl halide and one tertiary halide with a rearrangement-prone neighbour.
Compare transition energies/wavelengths of He+ vs H for analogous transitions; require combining Bohr-energy scaling with Rydberg formula to find which pair gives the same wavelength.
Four simple statements on NH3/PH3/AsH3 trends (boiling point, thermal stability, bond angle, basicity); pick the correct ones via codes.
For ideal-gas free expansion against vacuum, ask q, w, ΔU and ΔH — pure first-law sign/concept check, no numbers.

slots.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slots.brief: Give four isomeric alkenes (with cis/trans and substitution variation) and rank by heat of hydrogenation; students must translate stability ordering into ΔH values.
Rank three species (e.g., SF4, XeF4, ClF3-type set) by number of lone pairs on central atom and match to geometry; test VSEPR counting.
Match four named drugs (e.g., aspirin, paracetamol, equanil, morphine class) to their therapeutic use category; pick the odd/incorrect pairing.
Give two octahedral complexes of the same metal ion but different ligands from opposite ends of the spectrochemical series; ask which is high-spin and compare unpaired electrons.
Ask why H2O2 is stored in dark/waxed bottles with a stabilizer — simple conceptual recall of its decomposition and catalysis.
Aldohexose undergoes Kiliani–Fischer chain extension; ask how many stereoisomeric products form, which pairs are epimers/diastereomers, and which are optically active — demanding stereo-reasoning.
Combustion analysis of a hydrocarbon + oxygen mixture with volume contraction data (CO2 and H2O measured); find the mole fraction of fuel in the original mixture — multi-step stoichiometry.
Unsymmetrical ether (aryl–alkyl type) treated with excess HI; ask the organic products and why the aryl–O bond does not cleave — SN2 vs SN1 reasoning at harder level.

slots.subtopic: Basicity of amines in aqueous vs gas phase
slots.brief: Rank a set including aniline, ethylamine, guanidine-type and an amide-related nitrogen by basicity in water; must combine inductive, resonance and solvation effects.
Rank five radicals (alkyl, allylic, benzylic with substituent variation) by stability; simple concept with substitution-pattern twist.
Give rate constants at two temperatures and ask for activation energy plus the temperature at which the rate doubles — requires logarithmic manipulation of the two-point Arrhenius form.
Identify which of four aldehydes undergoes Cannizzaro reaction — check for absence of α-hydrogens.
Show a Fischer projection of a chiral molecule in the figure; assign R/S after a stated 90° rotation of the projection and identify the enantiomer/diastereomer among options.
Match defect types (Schottky, Frenkel, metal-excess, metal-deficiency) with examples and effects on density/conductivity at moderate level.
Gaseous equilibrium (e.g., PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 or AB2 type) starting from pure reactant at given total pressure; compute α from Kp with a quadratic — full ICE algebra.
For a specified exothermic gas-phase equilibrium, predict direction of shift on temperature/pressure/catalyst/inert-gas addition at constant volume — pure concept, easy statements.
Ask the shape/hybridisation of XeF4 and XeOF4-type species; count lone pairs via VSEPR and pick correct geometry option.
Electron accelerated through a potential difference; compute de Broglie wavelength using the KE–V relation — moderate plug-in.
Identify the glycosidic linkage and monosaccharide units of sucrose/maltose/lactose and which are reducing — mixed recall with a small reasoning element.
Two gases effuse through the same pinhole; use time or distance data to find the molar mass ratio of an unknown gas — moderate ratio computation.

slots.subtopic: van 't Hoff factor and complexes / isotonic solutions
slots.brief: Compare osmotic pressure of an electrolyte/complex solution with a given dissociation/association degree against a nonelectrolyte; solve for i and then concentration — hard multi-step colligative computation.

Given three lanthanide ions (e.g., Ln3+ series), compute spin-only vs orbital contribution and pick which has the maximum magnetic moment — requires electron-counting in f orbitals and trend reasoning.
Show a reaction scheme in the figure: an alkyl halide dehydrohalogenated, alkene converted with HBr (Markovnikov/peroxide cases), then substitution — identify the final product.
Three alcohols (1°, 2°, 3° including a cyclic one) subjected to Lucas test; predict turbidity order with time and explain via carbocation stability.
Give a diene/trisubstituted alkene in the figure; ozonolysis under reductive workup — ask which carbonyl fragments form, including how many moles of a specific product per mole.
Figure shows log(x/m) vs log P straight line; extract the slope, interpret what it means about saturation, and identify valid Freundlich statements.
Evaluate statements on maximum/minimum oxidation states across the 3d series (why Mn max is +7, why Cu +2 vs +1 stability) — moderate reasoning, pick the true set.
Four orderings of electron gain enthalpy across groups/periods (with Cl vs F anomaly, noble gases); identify which order is wrong — higher-order trend analysis.

slots.subtopic: Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant from cell EMF
slots.brief: Given E°cell for a specified n-electron cell at a non-standard temperature, compute ΔG° and K via ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT lnK — careful unit/log arithmetic.

Three complexes given with ligands/metal ions; determine hybridisation (d2sp3 vs sp3d2), spin state and magnetic moment — must first assign metal oxidation states, then apply VBT at higher difficulty.

slots.subtopic: Structure of oxides of phosphorus / hydrolysis of PCl3-type halides
slots.brief: Predict hydrolysis products of a p-block trichloride/pentachloride with balanced equation and structural reasoning (why PCl5 gives two anions in solution) — hard mixed concept.

slots.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slots.brief: Figure shows a small reaction-cycle or property chart of Li vs Mg; verify which listed similarities (nitride formation, carbonate decomposition, flame colour) are genuine — easy statement check.
Given limiting molar conductivities of some strong electrolytes, construct Λ° of a weak electrolyte (e.g., CH3COOH or a sparingly soluble salt) by linear combination — moderate numerical.

Order a set of species like O2, O2+, O2−, O22− and NO+ by bond length/bond order using MO reasoning, combined with a resonance-bond-length comparison (e.g., carbonate C–O bonds) — tough multi-species ranking.
Give the formula of a mixed-ligand coordination compound; pick the correct IUPAC name with proper ligand order, oxidation-state notation and geometric prefixes.
Pick a synonym for a moderately advanced descriptive adjective (e.g., 'candid', 'arduous') used in a short context sentence.
Five-sentence paragraph on science/history with first and last sentences fixed; order middle PQRS parts that hinge on a pronoun link and a contrast marker.
Complex sentence where a collective/quantity noun ('the committee', 'one of the...') is separated from its verb by an intervening phrase; spot the agreement error among four parts.
Single-blank sentence with a clear positive/negative tone cue; choose the fitting common word like 'meticulous' vs 'negligent'.
Simple sentence with a fixed prepositional collocation (e.g., 'afraid ___', 'insist ___'); pick the correct preposition.
Difficult double-blank vocabulary completion where tone shifts mid-sentence (concession followed by contrast); both blanks must fit logically and stylistically.
Long sentence mixing past perfect, simple past and a time clause; the trap options look wrong but the correct answer is 'no error', testing confidence in tense rules.
Simple, everyday word (e.g., 'abundant', 'brave'); choose the option closest in meaning.
Four/five jumbled sentences on a current-affairs or environmental theme; identify the correct opening sentence and full order using logical connectors and chronological clues.
Give an idiom like 'to let the cat out of the bag' in a mini-context; select the correct figurative meaning.
Sentence using simple past with 'since/for' time expressions; choose the option that corrects it to present perfect/present perfect continuous.
Convert a simple present/past declarative sentence with one object from active to passive; all four options are passive forms differing in auxiliary or object order.
Moderate-level word (e.g., 'frugal', 'candid', 'transient'); pick the option most nearly opposite in meaning.

Give a long word (e.g., a compound social-science term) and ask how many meaningful English words of exactly N letters can be formed using its letters without repetition; difficulty 5/5 so use a 12+ letter word and a strict letter-availability constraint.

Two interleaved alpha-numeric components (letters following a positional-value rule and numbers following separate arithmetic), ask for the next term combining both; add a twist like letters shifting by +2, -1 alternately to justify 4/5.
Two simple universal statements (All A are B, No B are C) with four conclusion options; 1/5 difficulty so conclusions follow directly and only one is valid.

Four letter clusters where three share a common property (e.g., letters all consecutive in the alphabet, or same positional-value sum) and one violates it; 3/5 so hide the property behind letter positions rather than obvious words.
Pointing-photo style statement chain ("he is the son of my grandfather's only child") asking the exact relation; 1/5 so keep it to 2-3 clear steps with a definite answer like "father" or "nephew".

Word pair where the analogy uses letter positional values (e.g., a word mapped by adding a fixed number to each letter's alphabet position); 3/5 so the underlying rule needs one inference step, and options include plausible distractor pairs.

A word coded by shifting each letter a variable but patterned number of steps (e.g., +1, +2, +3 progressively); ask the code for a new word following the same shift pattern; 2/5 so the pattern is easy to spot after one example.
Given a general second-degree equation, complete the square to identify the conic's centre/eccentricity-type parameters.
Words from letters of a given word where two specific letters must always be together and one letter never occupies an end position.
Given direction ratios of two lines, test whether they intersect; if so find the point of intersection.
Given z satisfying a quadratic-like relation, compute |z| and argument from modulus–conjugate identity 1/z = z̄/|z|².
Evaluate a 3×3 determinant by splitting entries into sums and using row/column operations to factor.
Direct integration by parts of a simple product (polynomial × exponential/trig); one application suffices.
Solve a homogeneous first-order DE using y = vx substitution and obtain the general solution.
Compute a definite integral via a simple u-substitution with adjusted limits.
Find the number of functions (or onto functions) from one finite set onto another using surjection counting.
Find the equation of a circle passing through two given points with a specified radius or centre on a given line.
Compute real/imaginary parts of an expression of the form z + 1/z using conjugate and modulus relations.
Classical probability with a small sample space (dice/cards); find probability of a compound event, possibly using independence.
Binomial distribution: given mean and variance (or two probability values), recover n and p, then compute a specific probability.
Two lines given in vector form; check coplanarity via scalar triple product and compute shortest distance if skew.
Count selections of a committee/team with at least one of each category, broken into cases by composition.
Simplify a vector triple product a×(b×c) using the standard identity and evaluate a resulting dot/scalar quantity.
Given f(x) a rational function, find its range using discriminant method for a quadratic in x.
Probability of at least one of several independent events using complement counting; e.g., system reliability or 'at least one'.
Find the domain of a composite/square-root rational function as an intersection of conditions.

slots.subtopic: Cross product and angle between vectors
slots.brief: Given vectors with dot product equal to cross-product magnitude, determine the angle between them.
Solve a linear first-order ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) using the integrating factor method.
For a discrete data set, compute mean deviation about the median from a short table of values.
Two related quantities changing with time (e.g., ladder sliding, water level rising); differentiate an implicit relation and evaluate at a given instant.
Differentiate a simple inverse trig function after simplifying with a substitution.
Solve a trigonometric equation combining sin and cos (reducible via t-formulas or auxiliary angle) and write the general solution.
Solve a rational inequality using a wavy-curve/sign-chart method and give the solution set.
Use differentials to estimate the percentage error in a computed quantity (area/volume) from an error in a measured variable.
Piecewise-defined function: find the unknown parameter so the function is continuous (and comment on differentiability) at the joining point.
Use the onto-function counting formula with inclusion–exclusion to count surjections between two small sets.
Given a symmetric relation between roots of a quadratic, form the equation using sum and product of roots.
For an implicit curve, find the equation of tangent/normal or dy/dx at a given point without solving for y.
Evaluate a straightforward definite integral of a standard trig/algebraic form using known antiderivatives.
For a system of linear equations, find the condition on a parameter for infinitely many solutions and then a solution property.
Evaluate a composite inverse trig expression (like tan⁻¹ inside another inverse) using the right-triangle method and identity substitution.
Find the equation of a line through the intersection of two given lines satisfying an extra condition (parallel/perpendicular to a third line).

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a point reflected in a given line; then check a distance or midpoint property.
For a pair of lines through origin given by a homogeneous second-degree equation, find the angle between them.
For a matrix A given explicitly, compute A² and use a relation to evaluate a scalar (e.g., trace/determinant) of a power or polynomial in A.
Find a specific term (or term independent of x) in a binomial expansion by equating exponents in the general term.
Investigate continuity and differentiability of a piecewise function at a point; find parameter(s) and check derivative existence via one-sided limits.
Use the property of definite integrals (f(x)+f(a−x)) to evaluate a definite integral of a trig/algebraic function.
Find the equation of a parabola from its focus and directrix (or vice versa).
Compute the area between two curves (line and parabola/circle) requiring intersection points and a proper definite integral.
Sum an arithmetico-geometric series to n terms or infinity using the shift-and-subtract method.

slots.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slots.brief: Find the range/maximum of an expression of the form a sin θ + b cos θ + c using the auxiliary-angle amplitude bound.
